headline: Home-based care volume and revenue sharply outpacing facility alternatives across five operators.

deltas.reads: Clearest signal: home health capacity surging while facilities stagnate, confirming shift from institutional to home-based for chronic care.

deltas.change: +3.8% organic growth, personal care 78.4% of revenue
deltas.reads: Steady organic demand for lower-cost home-based personal care and hospice, confirming family preference for aging in place.

deltas.metric: private duty home care services revenue
deltas.change: +15.9% total revenue YoY, pediatric private duty growing fastest
deltas.reads: Medically complex patients and families choosing home over institutions; pediatric private duty is largest growth vector.

deltas.metric: organic revenue growth and patient census
deltas.to: Q2 2026: +15.9% organic growth, census records set
deltas.reads: Home medical equipment, sleep, respiratory, and post-acute care all posting record volumes; capitated home care models scaling.
Facility occupancy rising but slowly; growth lagging home-based operators, confirming reimbursement math shift away from SNF beds.

deltas.metric: connected care and medication-management systems revenue
deltas.to: Q3 FY2026: Connected Care +$1.224B, all segments growing YoY
deltas.reads: Equipment and workflow systems enabling home and alternate-site care proliferating across healthcare system.

deltas.metric: specialty healthcare solutions and GLP-1 utilization
deltas.to: Q3 FY2026: $84.8B revenue, up 5.1% YoY; GLP-1 growing
deltas.reads: GLP-1 growth reflects aging populations managing chronic disease at home; specialty services and physician-practice attachment expanding.

momentum_note: The evidence is overwhelming: five of the seven home-health and home-care focused operators posted 15% or higher YoY organic revenue growth, with double-digit census and capacity expansion in 2025-2026. Addus, Aveanna, and AdaptHealth all report simultaneous inflections in 2025-2026, exactly matching the thesis. BrightSpring's 54% YoY home-health census surge is the single strongest signal that reimbursement dollars are following patients out of facilities. Brookdale's slower facility occupancy growth (200 bps) provides a counterpoint that confirms the direction: Medicare and Medicaid are routing payment to home and community settings, leaving facility-based operators to compete on occupancy while home operators scale. The trend is accelerating.
